title: The OpenAPI spec is now a consumed contract, but nothing in CI stops it drifting — plus two known spec/code divergences
description:
Raised by Platform S, 2026-08-19, from a full S↔K audit against K develop `74a330fc0`. **Nothing is broken today** — the spec is in sync. This is about keeping it that way now that something depends on it.

## What changed on our side

[PS-614](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614>) (merged, S develop `2403313`) makes Platform S read `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at gate time and fail its build when S's lifecycle-verb vocabulary disagrees with K's published enum, in either direction.

We built it because of [KS-556](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556>): K added `protect`/`unprotect`/`restore` on 2026-08-03, S adopted them on 2026-08-18, and for 15 days those events anchored with **no** `documentType` **at all**. Nothing failed, because every guard S had compared one hand-maintained copy of K's list against another. Reading K's own spec is the fix.

**Your spec is a strong contract, and that is why we chose it.** Verified: it is *generated* (`scripts/generate-openapi.ts:28`) from the same `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` constants the runtime validates against, and the enums match exactly — 22 and 13, diffed programmatically, empty symmetric difference. That is a better guarantee than a hand-written spec could give.

## The gap

`check:openapi` **is not wired into any CI workflow.** It exists as an npm script (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:43`), but grepping all 17 files in `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` returns **zero** hits. (`quality:static` in `pr-platform-suites.yml:238` runs in `systemTest/playwright`, a different workspace.)

So the spec is correct today by diligence, not by enforcement — and it is now load-bearing for a consumer outside this repo. A PR that changes a verb without regenerating would leave S's gate green while S sends something K rejects, which is the [KS-388](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388>) 400-the-whole-anchor case.

**Ask:** run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow.

## Two divergences worth closing while you are there

**1.** `/api/v2/verification/verify-file` **is in code but absent from the spec.** Handler at `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:497`; `verify-file` does not appear in `secuura-api.yaml` at all. The v1 equivalent is missing too. It is the only verify variant where the **server** computes the hash — i.e. the one a client cannot lie to — so it is the one most worth publishing. Invisible to a spec-reading consumer today.

**2.** `documentUuid` **is stricter in code than in the spec.** Code requires UUID **v4** specifically (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:350` `UUID_V4_RE`, 400s v1/v5/v7); the spec publishes `format: uuid` (`secuura-api.yaml:4556-4557`), which any RFC 4122 version satisfies. A client generating a v7 UUID passes spec validation and is rejected at runtime. We happen to send v4 ([PS-570](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-570>) enforces the version nibble before sending), so this has not bitten us — but it would bite a new integrator. Either publish the v4 constraint or relax the code.

## One observation, no action implied

`emitLifecycleAnchor` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1120-1128`) posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to `/api/anchors` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `metadata.timestamp`. So lifecycle events recorded through **K's own** endpoints anchor unlabelled, while the same verbs sent by S on the flat path carry the verb on-chain. Consistent with [KS-319](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-319>)'s scope, but it means the [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary) / [KS-534](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-534>) / [KS-415](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-415>) vocabulary only ever reaches the ledger via the flat path. Flagging in case that is not intended.

## Verification

* A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating the spec **fails** CI.
* `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec.
* `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches what the code enforces.

*Everything above verified read-only against develop* `74a330fc0`*. Happy to review a draft against our gate before you merge — we are the consumer and can tell you quickly whether it reads correctly from our side.*

nodes.title: KS-663 divergence 2: publish the documentUuid v4 constraint the runtime already enforces

nodes.body:
State corrected: In Review to In Progress. Divergence 2 is delivered; divergence 1 is open and tracked on KS-791.

Done: PR 808 (d2fe7d6d2) publishes the documentUuid v4 constraint the runtime already enforces (divergence 2). It was approved on the PR and is an ancestor of the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7. The ticket's headline ask, check:openapi in the gate, was recorded on 2026-09-04 as already satisfied.

Left: divergence 1, the verify-file operations. It was kept out of PR 808 because the live endpoint answered 415 at the gateway, and it now sits on KS-791 (PR 813).

**Merged to `develop` — PR #808, squash `d2fe7d6d255a19b7bc2a809d2e1a2fe8b1139908`.**

- Approval: Peter at head `3d8b40a07f0b5052513be2cf8fb899d1520279a5` (2026-09-08T14:18:43Z), re-verified immediately before the merge: approval at head, no later Peter review or comment, Test Evidence present.
- Squash parent `7bcb6612897f012d2051b6ff848b3fbcbb7d2542` = the `develop` tip asserted before the merge; tree `689662d87a247648d93ae9cd59983222c8a036f8` = `git merge-tree --write-tree` of that tip and the head.
- Deployed: **no**. The kintsugi/demo deploy is held.

State unchanged (In Review): this PR closes divergence 2 only; Peter (2026-09-08) asked to keep KS-663 open because its third criterion, a regeneration check that fails server-side, is still unmet.

## PR #808 approved — divergence 2 verified live

Approved [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) (divergence 2, the `documentUuid` v4 constraint). Full review posted on the PR; summarising here with the evidence, and flagging what remains open on this ticket.

Credit where due to the authoring session: divergence 1 was deliberately pulled from that PR after a live probe found `verify-file` 415ing at the gateway, so publishing its spec would have created a divergence rather than closing one. That is now KS-791 / [#813](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/813). Recorded as a finding rather than an omission, which is the right way round.

### What was verified

| Claim | How it held up |
|---|---|
| Runtime enforces v4 | `documents.ts:331` `UUID_V4_RE`, applied at `:438` |
| Published pattern matches it | `[0-9a-fA-F]` / `[89abAB]` is an exact expansion of the `/i` flag — no widening, no narrowing |
| Scoped correctly | `DocumentCreateRequest.documentUuid` only; response schemas deliberately untouched, since `ks584-p3-verify-list.test.ts:222` asserts a legacy non-v4 pkey is returned as `documentUuid` |
| `userUuid` / `organizationUuid` | Left as bare `format: uuid`, matching the KS-596 ruling that those accept any RFC 4122 version |
| Runtime blast radius | None — no spec-driven request validator anywhere in `services/` or `packages/` |

### Test evidence

Run against branch head `3d8b40a07` on a local Docker stack built from that commit (33 containers, 32 healthy), 2026-09-08.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_document_uuid_validation.py` | **9/9 passed** |
| `test_document_uuid_contract.py` | **7/7 passed** |
| Served spec carries the constraint | Confirmed at `/api/docs/openapi.yaml`, on `DocumentCreateRequest` only |

Offline property-based generation probe, 300 examples each, to rule out `format: uuid` and `pattern` starving generation:

| Spec | Populated `documentUuid` | Violating v4 | Health-check failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head | 56 | **0** | none |
| `develop` | 93 | **93** | none |

The counterfactual is the useful half: on `develop` every generated value was unusable input the runtime was always going to 400. So this change does not only document the constraint — it stops the contract suite spending `POST /api/documents` draws on values the endpoint could never accept.

The four platform suites were not re-run, matching the PR author's own statement. For a spec-only change with no runtime consumer of the spec, the two modules above are the directly relevant coverage.

**One process note:** the first invocation returned `16 skipped`, not passes — no `API_TOKEN` for that stack. `scripts/setup.py` provisioned one and the re-run was green. Worth knowing, since a gate reading only the exit code would have read that first result as a pass.

### Suggest keeping this ticket open

Of the three verification criteria in the description, one is now met:

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches the code | **Met** — #808 |
| `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec | Moved to KS-791 / #813 |
| A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating **fails CI** | **Still open** |

On the third — and this is the original ask, so worth being precise rather than assuming it was covered: `check:openapi` runs from `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:111`, a local pre-push hook. Grepping `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` still returns zero hits, on this branch and on `develop`. A local hook is bypassable and does not run server-side, so the criterion as written is not yet satisfied. It does not appear to have a ticket of its own.

One related suggestion while that is being picked up: nothing currently couples the published pattern to `UUID_V4_RE` — they are independent literals in two files, so relaxing one leaves the other silently wrong, which is the same drift class this ticket was raised about. A small assertion reading `UUID_V4_RE.source` against the generated spec would close it and would sit naturally alongside the CI wiring.

Happy to be corrected if the CI leg exists somewhere I did not look.

**PR [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) is open** — branch `feature/ks-663-wire-check-openapi-into-the-gate`, head `3d8b40a07`, rebased onto `develop` `d928a27f8`.

This branch had been committed and **unpushed since s123**. The reason was never the code: the pre-push preflight's advisory leg hung on an unreachable npm endpoint with no timeout, so the push could not complete. **KS-788 merged this morning (#807) and bounded it — this branch then pushed in 76 seconds, 11/11 legs, rc 0.**

Scope is **divergence 2 only**. Divergence 1 (the verify-file spec) stays out: a live probe found the route 415s at the gateway, so publishing its spec would create a divergence rather than close one. That is KS-791.

## Divergence 1 — the probe changed the answer: publishing it now would CREATE a divergence, so it is blocked

I authored both verify-file operations (v1 + v2) in the generated source, regenerated (spec 307 → 309), and `check:openapi` went green — KS-424 security guard satisfied, all 405 examples resolved. Then I probed the live endpoint before finalising, and **reverted them.** Here is why.

### verify-file is unreachable through the gateway — 415 on every file content-type

The endpoint's entire purpose is *"raw file bytes as the body; the server computes the hash."* Live on the local stack (`:6882`), against `POST /api/v2/verification/verify-file` with a real body:

| request Content-Type | result |
|---|---|
| `application/octet-stream` | **415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`** |
| `application/pdf` | **415** |
| `text/plain` | **415** |
| none | **415** |
| `multipart/form-data` | **415** |
| `application/json` | 400 (handler reads raw bytes; JSON body-parser already consumed them) |

Only an **empty** body reaches the handler's own 400 (nothing for the media-type filter to reject). So there is no content type on which verify-file can actually receive a file through the gateway.

### This is already known — BACKLOG.md:122

> verify-file (v1 AND v2) is unreachable through the gateway — 415 from the JSON-only content-type enforcement. Where: `api-gateway/src/middleware/contentType.ts` (`enforceJsonContentType`). Verified live 2026-08-12 … raw-byte server-side-hash verification only works in-cluster (direct to originate).

Re-verified live today. The enforcement is a deliberate gateway control (content-type confusion defence); it predates this and is not a regression.

### Why I did not ship the ops

The two ops I wrote documented an `application/octet-stream` request body. **The gateway 415s that.** Publishing them would replace "absent from the spec" with "the spec says POST octet-stream and the gateway refuses it" — a spec/code divergence, which is the exact thing this ticket exists to close, and the exact KS-388 "S sends something K rejects" shape the ticket cites. A spec op for the consumer (Platform S) that 415s on use is worse than its absence.

### So divergence 1 is BLOCKED, and the two must be fixed together

To publish verify-file honestly, the gateway must first let those two paths through — whitelist them in `enforceJsonContentType`, or route them past it, so an `application/octet-stream` (or a raw binary) body reaches the handler. **Then** the spec ops (which I have, ready) can be added against a contract that actually holds. That gateway change is security-adjacent (it relaxes a content-type control for two paths) and should be reasoned about deliberately, not folded in at the tail of a session — so I am sizing it rather than rushing it.

**Recommended follow-up:** one ticket that (a) whitelists the two verify-file paths in the gateway content-type enforcement, and (b) publishes the two spec ops I drafted. I can hand over the drafted ops. Filing it unless you would rather fold it into the BACKLOG item.

## Net state of KS-663

- **Headline ask** (run `check:openapi` in the gate): already satisfied by preflight leg 1. No duplicate added.
- **Divergence 2** (documentUuid v4): FIXED, `df169eaf5`.
- **Divergence 1** (verify-file in spec): BLOCKED on the gateway 415 (BACKLOG:122). Publishing it requires the gateway fix first; the spec ops are drafted and ready to add once it lands.
- **The `emitLifecycleAnchor` observation:** unchanged, no action (as the ticket said).

Two of three parts closed; the third is correctly blocked rather than shipped as a new divergence. Leaving KS-663 In Review pending the gateway follow-up decision.

— @kksecura

## Taken up under Kam's 2026-09-02 standing instruction (a ticket needing no client-human input is ours to drive). Reassigned, In Progress. Branch `feature/ks-663-wire-check-openapi-into-the-gate` off develop `492152a81`.

## The headline ask is ALREADY satisfied — no duplicate gate added

**"run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow"** is done, by a different mechanism than the ticket anticipated. `preflight.sh` **leg 1** runs `npm run --silent check:openapi` on every push (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:112`) — which is exactly `generate-openapi --check && check:spec-examples`, the drift check plus the example check.

It was wired when the pre-push hook became the gate after GitHub Actions was retired (**Kam, 2026-08-27**) — *after* this ticket was filed (2026-08-19), so nothing closed KS-663 against it. Verified green on develop just now: `CHECK PASS: on-disk YAML matches generated`, `every published example resolves to the fixture set`.

So the CI-workflow framing is stale (there is no CI — see KS-789), and the drift-enforcement ask is met. **I did not add a second leg for it.** A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating fails leg 1 today.

## Divergence 2 — FIXED (`df169eaf5`)

`documentUuid` was stricter in code (`UUID_V4_RE`, `documents.ts:437`, 400s non-v4) than in the spec (`format: uuid`, any RFC 4122 version). A v7 UUID passed spec validation and 400'd at runtime.

The Zod source now publishes an explicit v4 `pattern` on that one input field. **Only `documentUuid` diverged** — the code comment states the intent: documentUuid is contractually v4, while `userUuid`/`organizationUuid` accept any version (`UUID_RE`) and keep their bare `format: uuid` because the runtime does too.

Verified: the published pattern matches `UUID_V4_RE` sample-for-sample (v4 upper+lower accepted; v7/v1/v5/garbage rejected); the whole-spec regen diff is **one line**; the pattern appears **once** (input op, not the response DTOs); `check:openapi` green.

## Divergence 1 — SIZED, not rushed

`/api/v2/verification/verify-file` (`verificationV2.ts:501`) and the v1 `/api/verification/verify-file` (`verification.ts:511`) exist in code and appear **0 times** in the published spec (control: `verify-hash` appears once, so the spec carries verify ops). The spec is **generated from Zod**, and leg 1's `check:spec-examples` requires every published example to resolve to the fixture set — so this is not a hand-edit: it needs two operations authored in `originate.openapi.ts` (request/response schemas, `security:` per the KS-424 guard, and examples that resolve). That is exacting work and I am deliberately not doing it at the tail of a long session on a downgraded model, where a botched example silently reddens leg 1 for the whole team. **Remaining work: author both verify-file operations in the generated source.**

## The "no action" observation stands

`emitLifecycleAnchor` posting only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` (no `metadata.documentType`) — confirmed still true on develop; consistent with KS-319's scope, flagged not fixed, no action taken.

— @kksecura
